lesson_yaml:
schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: java-xpath-evaluate-inputsource-xxe
title: XPath.evaluate on a raw InputSource parses XML without XXE hardening
summary: 'Calling javax.xml.xpath.XPath.evaluate(expression, InputSource, returnType) makes the JAXP implementation
  parse the XML with its own default, unhardened parser. External entities and DTDs are then resolved,
  which allows XXE (local file disclosure, SSRF and denial of service). The fix parses the input first
  with a hardened DocumentBuilderFactory and evaluates the XPath against the resulting DOM.

  '

rule:
  message: 'XPath evaluation directly on an InputSource lets the default JAXP parser process the XML,
    including

    external entities and DTDs (XXE). Parse the input with a hardened DocumentBuilderFactory first

    and evaluate the XPath against the resulting DOM node.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: $XPATH.evaluate($EXPR, (InputSource $IS), ...)
    - pattern: $XPATH.evaluate($EXPR, new InputSource(...), ...)
    - pattern: $XPATH.evaluateExpression($EXPR, (InputSource $IS), ...)
    - pattern: $XPATH.evaluateExpression($EXPR, new InputSource(...), ...)
fix:
  guidance: Do not pass an InputSource (or a stream or SAX source) straight to XPath.evaluate. Create
    the DocumentBuilderFactory through DocumentBuilderFactoryUtils.newInstance(), which disables DTDs
    and external entities. Parse the input into a Document, then evaluate the expression against that
    DOM node.
  example: 'DocumentBuilderFactory factory = DocumentBuilderFactoryUtils.newInstance();

    factory.setNamespaceAware(true);

    Document document = factory.newDocumentBuilder().parse(inputSource);

    Object result = xpath.evaluate(expression, document, returnType);

    '
